 Nvidia stock dropped sharply on Monday morning as the company began investigating CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital relationship.
 The stock dropped 8% at the open Monday, falling to around $171 per share and wiping as much as $360 billion from Friday's closing market capitalization of $4.5 trillion. By just after midday E.T., the stock was trading at $177, a loss of around 5% from Friday's close.
 The stock has already fallen 20% over the past month.
 Tech stocks have faced a broader sell-off amid investor concerns that AI infrastructure won't be built as quickly as hoped, sparked by neocloud firms' high debt levels and the Democrats' big gains in the midterm elections, which could slow data center construction.
 Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and has overseen a meteoric rise, with the company worth trillions since the AI boom supercharged demand for its chips.
 As its founder and longtime CEO, Huang is pivotal to Nvidia's ongoing success, and Monday's share price decline likely reflects concerns the scandal could lead to his departure from the chipmaker.
 "The so-called 'key-man risk' looms large here, and it's doubtful markets have adequately priced it in," Mohamed El-Erian, the legendary bond investor, wrote in an X post.
 "This will not be easy for the board to navigate."
 As one of its founders, Huang has a substantial financial stake in Nvidia, which has ballooned in value as the company has grown. As of Friday's market close, he has a net worth of $155 billion, making him the 10th richest person on earth, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

 Huang's Nvidia stake fell in value by as much as $13 billion to around $138 billion on Monday morning, Business Insider calculated based on his most recent ownership disclosure.
 Revelations about Huang's personal life
 In late October, The New York Times reported that American intelligence agencies discovered that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang , a Chinese citizen and former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company.
 US officials suspected her company was steering Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China, and concluded that she was a Chinese intelligence asset, the report said.
 At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told the Times, "Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected."
 On Sunday, Jensen Huang sent a note to staff acknowledging he had been "unfaithful" to his wife, Lori Huang , to whom he's been married for over 40 years.
 Nvidia's board of directors opened an investigation into whether its CEO was the target of a "foreign intelligence effort."
 "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," he wrote. "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully."
